money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The official currency of Kosovo is the euro. You need to declare amounts over 10,000 euro or equivalent when you arrive. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't, you may be fined. Although credit card use is increasing, Kosovo is a cash economy based on the euro. ATMs are readily available throughout Kosovo, and users should take normal precautions to safeguard their PIN when using them. It's a good idea to carry some cash, including for minor purchases.

culture-cycles.public_holidays: Law No. 03/L-064 on Official Holidays: 1 and 2 January; 7 January (Orthodox Christmas); 17 February (Independence Day); 9 April (Constitution Day); 1 May; 9 May (Europe Day); first day of Eid al-Fitr; first day of Eid al-Adha; Catholic and Orthodox Easter Mondays; 25 December. A holiday on a weekend moves to the next working day. The government publishes each year's calendar (the 2025 one came from the Ministry of Internal Affairs).
moving_calendars: Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha follow the lunar calendar; the official calendar warns dates can change and a second notice is issued.
Catholic and Orthodox Easter Mondays are both holidays and sometimes fall on the same day (21 April 2025).
protocol_notes: Memorial days in the law include 28 November (Albanians' day), 12 June (Peace Day), 6 March (Veterans), 23 April (Turks), 8 April (Roma), 15 February (Ashkali), 28 September (Bosniaks) and 6 May (Gorani).
Smartraveller warns of celebratory gunfire on holidays and after sporting wins.
culture-cycles.note: The 2027 government calendar wasn't found yet (the law says it's issued by the end of October).
